q: There is Myanmar riddle 'Which is heavier, a viss of cotton (or) a viss of ____ ?'
e: There is Myanmar riddle 'Which is heavier, a viss of cotton (or) a viss of iron?'. Iron here means the metal in magnetite and the common magnetic element.

q: Density is the ratio of ____ to volume of a substance.
e: Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Density is the ratio of mass to ____ of a substance.
e: Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Density is the ____ quantity.
e: Density is the scalar quantity. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: The Greek alphabet used to represent density is ____.
e: The Greek alphabet used to represent density is $\rho$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in ____ ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).
e: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre (____).
e: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies involving kilogram.

q: In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per ____ ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$).
e: In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per mililitre ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$). The physics in this sentence is built around mililitre.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a ____ and volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.
e: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance and volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder. The physics in this sentence is built around balance.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance and volume can be measured using a ____.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the ____ depends on the temperature.
e: Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: If the volume changes, the ____ will change.
e: If the volume changes, the density will change. Density here means mass per unit volume. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.
